title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Practice: Constructing Perpendicular Lines
description: Practice identifying perpendicular lines, choosing tools, following construction steps, and checking right angles.

questions.question: Two lines are perpendicular if they intersect to form a ______ angle.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines meet to form right angles.

questions.question: What is the measure of the angle formed by perpendicular lines?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines form right angles, and a right angle measures 90 degrees.

questions.question: Which tool is most directly useful for marking a $90^\circ$ angle during construction?
questions.explanation: A protractor measures and marks angles, including 90 degrees.

questions.question: A perpendicular line must always be vertical on the page.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines can be rotated or slanted. The important fact is that they meet at 90 degrees.

questions.question: Write the symbol for perpendicular: AB ______ CD.
To construct a perpendicular through point P on line $\ell$ with a protractor, where should the protractor center go?
options: At the end of the ruler
questions.explanation: The new perpendicular must pass through P, so the right angle must be marked from P.

questions.question: A student draws a line through P that meets line $\ell$ at $87^\circ$. Explain whether the construction is perpendicular.
questions.correctAnswer: It is not perpendicular because a perpendicular line must form a 90-degree angle, not an 87-degree angle.
questions.explanation: A construction that is close to 90 degrees may look right, but perpendicular requires exactly 90 degrees.

questions.question: Point Q is not on line m. Describe the point called the foot of the perpendicular when constructing from Q to m.
questions.correctAnswer: The foot of the perpendicular is the point where the perpendicular segment from Q meets line m.
questions.explanation: For an off-line point, the foot is the meeting point on the original line.
